summary: DEFLATE (RFC 1951) and gzip (RFC 1952) in pure Mojo — no FFI, no dependencies.
description:
`deflate` compresses, `inflate` decompresses, and `inflate_at` decompresses
one stream out of several laid back to back, reporting where it ended.
`gunzip` decodes a `.gz` file (every member, CRC-32 and length checked),
`gunzip_at` one member of it, and `gzip` writes one. `GzipReader` and
`Inflater` are the streaming forms: they decode a window at a time, from
input that may still be arriving.

```mojo
from deflate import deflate, inflate

var packed = deflate(Span(data))    # List[UInt8], raw DEFLATE
var back = inflate(Span(packed))    # List[UInt8], == data
```

`inflate` and `deflate` streams are *raw*: no zlib (RFC 1950) header, no
gzip wrapper, no trailing checksum. Avro's `deflate` block codec is raw and
needs nothing more; gzip files go through `gunzip`.

modules.summary: gzip (RFC 1952) framing over the raw DEFLATE in `raw.mojo`.
modules.description:
`gunzip` decodes a whole `.gz` file: every member of a concatenated stream,
each one's header (all five flags: FTEXT, FHCRC, FEXTRA, FNAME, FCOMMENT)
parsed and skipped, and each one's CRC-32 and ISIZE checked against what it
decoded to. `gunzip_at` decodes one member and reports where it ended, as
`inflate_at` does for raw streams. `gzip` writes a single member.

The CRC-32 is the zlib/gzip one (reflected polynomial 0xEDB88320), slice-by-8
as in hashes.mojo's `crc32`. It is repeated here rather than imported so the
tin keeps no sibling dependency: a consumer still needs nothing but
`-I deflate.mojo/src`.

structs.name: GzipReader
structs.summary: A gzip file decoded a window at a time: every member of it, or just the first.
structs.description:
The streaming form of `gunzip`, over `Inflater`: `run` decodes until the
window (`output()`) holds `want` bytes, the input runs short or the file
ends; `compact` drops what the caller has used. The input may still be
arriving, and input already consumed may be discarded, exactly as for
`Inflater`. Headers, CRC-32s and ISIZEs are checked as `gunzip` checks
them, with the same messages; the CRC is folded in as output is
produced, so it covers bytes long since compacted away.

```mojo
var gz = GzipReader()
var have = 0  # how much of `data` has arrived
while True:
    var st = gz.run(Span(data)[:have], have == len(data), len(gz) + (1 << 20))
    parse(gz.output())
    _ = gz.compact(len(gz))
    if st == InflateStatus.FINISHED:
        break
    if st == InflateStatus.NEED_INPUT:
        have = ...  # wait for more
```

fields.name: inflater
fields.summary: Holds the window and the DEFLATE state of the member being decoded.

fields.name: member_at
fields.summary: Absolute input offset of the current member's header (for messages).

overloads.signature: def __init__(out self, capacity: Int = Int(1048576), multi_member: Bool = True)
overloads.summary: `capacity` is the window's starting size. With `multi_member` false, decoding stops after the first member, and whatever follows it is left alone (`input_used()` says where it ended).
Everything decoded and not yet compacted away.

overloads.signature: def compact(mut self, keep_from: Int) -> Int
overloads.summary: `Inflater.compact`: drop `output()[0:keep_from]` as far as back-references allow; return how many bytes went.
Members decoded and verified so far.
The window as a list, consuming the reader.
How many bytes of `data` the reader is done with; once finished, the offset just past the last trailer it read (or padding).
`Inflater.discard_input`: forget the input before `input_used()` and return how many bytes that is.

overloads.signature: def run(mut self, data: Span[UInt8], complete: Bool, want: Int = Int.MAX) -> InflateStatus
overloads.summary: Decode from `data` until the window holds `want` bytes: `OUTPUT`, `NEED_INPUT` or `FINISHED`, as `Inflater.run`. Raises what `gunzip` raises, once `complete` says no more input is coming (and on corruption before that).
`armv8-crc` or `slice-by-8`: which CRC-32 this build uses.
Decompress a gzip file: all of its members, concatenated.
overloads.description:
Each member's CRC-32 and length are verified. Zero bytes after the last
member are padding (as gzip(1) and Python's `gzip` accept); anything else
there raises, as does an empty input.

overloads.signature: def gunzip_at(data: Span[UInt8], mut end: Int) -> List[UInt8]
overloads.summary: Decompress the one gzip member at the start of `data`, verifying its CRC-32 and length, and set `end` to the offset just past its trailer.
overloads.description:
For walking a multi-member file one member at a time, so only one
member's output is held at once:

```mojo
var pos = 0
while pos < len(data):
    var end = 0
    var part = gunzip_at(Span(data)[pos:], end)
    pos += end
```

overloads.signature: def gzip(data: Span[UInt8], level: Int = Int(6)) -> List[UInt8]
overloads.summary: Compress `data` into a single gzip member.
overloads.description:
`level` 0 writes stored (uncompressed) DEFLATE blocks; 1 to 9 all use
`deflate`'s one fixed-Huffman strategy, so they produce the same bytes.
The header carries no name, comment or timestamp (MTIME 0, OS 255).

modules.summary: Raw DEFLATE (RFC 1951) — `inflate` and `deflate`, in pure Mojo.
modules.description:
*Raw* DEFLATE is the compressed stream on its own: no zlib (RFC 1950) header,
no gzip (RFC 1952) wrapper, no trailing checksum. A caller that needs one of
those framings parses it itself and hands the body here — Avro's `deflate`
block codec is raw already, and Parquet's `GZIP` codec is this plus a gzip
header and trailer.

Implementing it rather than binding zlib keeps the tin free of FFI and of any
sibling dependency, so a consumer needs nothing but `-I ../deflate.mojo/src`.

`inflate` handles all three block types (stored, fixed-Huffman,
dynamic-Huffman). `deflate` emits fixed-Huffman blocks from a single-slot
hash-chain LZ77 matcher — the same "fast" strategy `snappy.mojo` uses —
which keeps the encoder small.

aliases.name: MARGIN
aliases.summary: The input a block is started with when more is still to come (`run` with `complete=False`). zlib ends a block every 16 Ki or 32 Ki symbols, at most about 200 KB of input, so with 256 KiB in hand a block almost never runs past what has arrived; one that does is rolled back and decoded again once more input is there.

aliases.name: OUTPUT
aliases.summary: The window holds the output asked for (`n >= want`).

aliases.name: NEED_INPUT
aliases.summary: More input is needed before anything more can be decoded.

aliases.name: FINISHED
aliases.summary: The stream (every gzip member) has been decoded and checked.

structs.name: Inflater
structs.summary: A raw DEFLATE stream decoded a window at a time.
structs.description:
The output collects in a window, `output()`. `run` decodes
blocks until the window holds `want` bytes, the input runs short or the
stream ends; the caller uses what is there, then `compact`s away what it
no longer needs. The window keeps the last 32 KiB whatever is dropped,
since later back-references may reach that far.

The input may still be arriving. `run` takes the input so far and
whether that is all of it; a block that runs past the bytes there is
rolled back to its start and decoded again on a later call, with more.
The caller may drop input the inflater has finished with: see
`discard_input`.

```mojo
var inf = Inflater()
while True:
    var st = inf.run(Span(input), complete, want=len(inf) + (1 << 20))
    use(inf.output())
    _ = inf.compact(len(inf))
    if st == InflateStatus.FINISHED:
        break
    if st == InflateStatus.NEED_INPUT:
        ...  # append more to `input` (or set complete)
```

`inflate` and `inflate_at` are this with the whole input and a window
that is never compacted.

fields.name: pos
fields.summary: The next input byte not yet in the bit buffer, as an offset into the `data` passed to `run`.

fields.name: margin
fields.summary: Input to have in hand before starting a block while more is still to come (`MARGIN`). 0 starts every block at once and rolls back each one that outruns the input, which tests use.

fields.name: dropped_in
fields.summary: Input bytes `discard_input` has released: what `pos` is relative to.

fields.name: dyn_clen
fields.summary: A dynamic block's three codes, rebuilt in place block after block.

fields.name: lengths
fields.summary: Scratch for a dynamic block's code lengths.

overloads.summary: `capacity` is the window's starting size; it grows as needed.
The window: everything decoded and not yet compacted away.
`len(output())`.

overloads.signature: def compact(mut self, keep_from: Int) -> Int
overloads.summary: Drop `output()[0:keep_from]`, as far as back-references allow, and return how many bytes went: subtract it from any offsets into the window the caller holds.
Bytes decoded so far, compacted or not.
Whether the final block has been decoded.
The window as a list (trimmed to `n`), consuming the inflater.
How many bytes of `data` the inflater is done with. Once the stream has finished this is where it ended (rounded up to a byte), as `inflate_at` reports.
Forget the input before `input_used()` and return how many bytes that is: the next `run` must be passed `data` without them. A long stream can then be fed through a bounded input buffer.
Input consumed so far, discarded or not.

overloads.signature: def run(mut self, data: Span[UInt8], complete: Bool, want: Int = Int.MAX) -> InflateStatus
overloads.summary: Decode from `data` (the input so far, from where the last call left off unless `discard_input` said otherwise; all of it if `complete`) until the window holds `want` bytes.
overloads.description:
Returns `OUTPUT` when it does, `NEED_INPUT` when a block is waiting
for more input than `data` has, or `FINISHED` after the final block.
Raises on corrupt input, and on input that ends early once
`complete` is set.

overloads.summary: Decompress a raw DEFLATE stream.

overloads.signature: def inflate_at(data: Span[UInt8], mut end: Int) -> List[UInt8]
overloads.summary: Decompress a DEFLATE stream, and report where it ended.
overloads.description:
`end` is set to the offset of the first byte *after* the stream, rounded
up to a byte boundary. Callers with several streams back to back —
concatenated gzip members, for instance — need it to find the next one;
callers that do not can use `inflate`.

overloads.summary: Compress to a raw DEFLATE stream (one fixed-Huffman block).
